register.purpose: Where every record in this repository came from, what the host allows, and what the tool is therefore permitted to do with it.
how_to_read: robots: the file that was actually fetched, its HTTP status, a sha256 prefix of the body, and the verdict reached from it.
license: the terms the host publishes for the records, not the terms for the website.
policy.ai_input: may a record from this source be sent to the model layer (--llm)?
policy.record_source: may records from this source be used as label input at all?
decision: admitted, refused, or reference_only, with the reason in one sentence.
A refusal here is a result, not a gap. It is the same posture the pipeline takes on a missing field.

sources.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access

robots.notes: The API host publishes no robots.txt. The website host is behind a bot checkpoint, which is why the tool uses the documented API and never the website.

decision.reason: Documented open API, CC0 records, no key.

sources.name: The Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access

robots.notes: The API host disallows one crawler (Amazonbot) and nothing else. The museum's website separately sets Crawl-delay: 10 and Disallow: /api on its own host; the tool uses neither, and keeps a 0.5 s gap between API calls.

policy.notes: Records flagged CC0 by the API are filtered in at fetch time; the rest are dropped.

decision.reason: Documented open API, CC0 records, robots allows it.

robots.notes: Allow: / for user-agent *, but Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-train=no, use=reference, and a long Disallow list of training crawlers. Crawling for reference is permitted; AI training is not; ai-input is neither granted nor restricted, so the conservative reading applies.

policy.notes: Collection data carries no open licence, and the site answers non-browser clients with a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403). Getting past that challenge would be evasion, not permission.

decision.reason: No open licence for the records, ai-train=no in the content signals, and the site is bot-protected. Records may only enter through tools/import_records.py, supplied by a person who has legitimate access.

robots.notes: The request returns a 70-byte meta refresh to /Home.html rather than a robots file. Collection paths tried returned 404 with the same redirect. A missing robots.txt is not a grant, and nothing else on the site supplies one.

policy.notes: No robots policy, no open data licence, no API, and no reachable collection endpoint. There is no basis on which to harvest records, so none were.

decision.reason: No robots.txt, no open licence, no API. Records may only enter through tools/import_records.py, supplied by a person who has legitimate access.

robots.notes: Cloudflare managed challenge returned for every request from this network, with a browser user-agent and without one. The body is a challenge page, not a robots file, so no verdict can be reached. No hash is recorded: a challenge page is generated per request, so hashing it would report drift on every run without anything having changed. The status is the fact worth comparing.

policy.notes: The proposal names this museum as the fallback dataset. It stays named as the fallback: the licence and the API are right, the network path is not. Re-check with tools/check_sources.py before relying on it.

decision.reason: Declared fallback in the proposal. Not frozen because the API answers with a bot challenge from this network; nothing was attempted past the challenge.

robots.notes: The Action API host is allowed; only a list of known-bad crawlers is disallowed. The SPARQL host is a different matter: query.wikidata.org/robots.txt disallows /sparql and /bigdata outright, so no SPARQL query is used anywhere in this repository.

policy.notes: Rejected as a record source, not as a data source. An aggregator record has an inventory number and a material, but no credit line, so it cannot satisfy the five-field contract. Filling that field from the label's own wording would be the exact failure the tool exists to prevent.

decision.reason: Openly licensed and reachable, but an aggregator record cannot supply a credit line. Useful for cross-checking an object; not usable as label input.

robots.notes: The data is a CC0 bulk dump on GitHub, fetched as a file rather than crawled from the museum's site, so no robots policy applies to this project's access.

policy.notes: Admitted in principle; not frozen, because the dump is far larger than a 10-record corpus warrants and the repository keeps its data small on purpose.

decision.reason: CC0 and reachable, but nothing in the project needs a second bulk source yet.
